deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): ABC is a spherical triangle on the unit sphere with centre O, sides a, b, c and angles A, B, C. Gauss has shown that the common value
K = sin A sin b sin c = sin B sin a sin c = sin C sin a sin b
equals 6·Vol(OABC), six times the volume of the tetrahedron whose vertices are A, B, C and O. He has also shown K = 4 cot r · sin(a/2) sin(b/2) sin(c/2), where r is the spherical radius of the circle circumscribed about the spherical triangle.

This page gives a second, purely geometric expression for K, and through it a proof of the cot r formula.

(1) Claim: K = 4 cos r · sin 𝔞 · sin(b/2) · sin(c/2). Here 𝔞, 𝔟, 𝔠 are the angles of the plane (chord) triangle ABC, whose vertices are the same three points joined by straight chords.

(2) The sides of the chord triangle are the chords BC = 2 sin(a/2), CA = 2 sin(b/2), AB = 2 sin(c/2).

(3) Twice the area of the chord triangle is therefore CA·AB·sin 𝔞 = 4 sin 𝔞 sin(b/2) sin(c/2).

(4) The same plane triangle is the base of the pyramid OABC.
- The plane through A, B, C cuts the sphere in the small circle circumscribed about the spherical triangle. Its spherical radius is r.
- So the distance from O to that plane, i.e. the height of the pyramid, is cos r. (The plane circumradius is sin r.) This filling-in is mine but certain.
- Hence 6V = 6·(1/3)·Area·h = 2·Area·cos r = 4 cos r sin 𝔞 sin(b/2) sin(c/2).
- Gauss: 'woraus die Richtigkeit von selbst erhellt' (whence the correctness is self-evident).

(5) Implicit link to the previous page (my filling-in): the plane law of sines in the chord triangle with circumradius sin r gives 2 sin(a/2) / sin 𝔞 = 2 sin r, i.e. sin 𝔞 = sin(a/2)/sin r. Substituting into (4) gives K = 4 cot r sin(a/2) sin(b/2) sin(c/2). So this page supplies the proof of the cot r formula from the previous page.

(6) A struck-out remark says roughly: only the derivation of the formula marked ♂ (a reference sign that also appears in red in the margin of the facing page) would require a different figure.

(7) Below this is faint, largely illegible pencil text. It seems to mention angles and lines drawn from a point toward the arcs a, b, c. It cannot be reconstructed reliably.
errors: No mathematical errors. The step 'height = cos r' is asserted without comment. It is correct because the plane ABC cuts the sphere in the circumcircle of spherical radius r.
The cot r formula of the previous page needs the chord-triangle law of sines, sin 𝔞 = sin(a/2)/sin r, to follow from this page. Gauss leaves this step implicit.

results.what: 6·Vol(OABC) = sin A sin b sin c for a spherical triangle on the unit sphere (triple product of the vertex vectors)
results.modern_name: volume of a trihedral tetrahedron / polar sine (von Staudt's 'Sinus' of a solid angle)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler/Lagrange era (triple product); polar sine named by von Staudt 1842

results.what: 6V = 4 cos r sin 𝔞 sin(b/2) sin(c/2) via the chord triangle as base and cos r as height
results.modern_name: base-times-height volume of the tetrahedron spanned by the centre and the chord triangle

results.what: Consequence: tan r = 2 sin(a/2) sin(b/2) sin(c/2) / (sin A sin b sin c / 2), i.e. K = 4 cot r Π sin(half sides)
results.modern_name: formula for the circumradius of a spherical triangle

deep.surprise_reason: The material is classical spherical trigonometry: a tetrahedron-volume interpretation and the circumradius formula proved by an elegant chord-triangle argument. It is neat, but it is standard and contains nothing beyond what was known around 1800.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Auch ist dieselbe' followed by a struck word (probably 'Größe'), not a repeated 'dieselbe'.
The angles are written as Fraktur 𝔞, 𝔟, 𝔠 (preceded by an angle sign ∡), so the formula reads sin 𝔞 rather than Greek sin α.

In the struck final passage, 'Formel 𝔍' should be 'Formel ♂'. The Mars-like reference sign is also drawn in red in the margin of the facing page. The passage reads roughly 'Bloss die Ableitung der Formel ♂ würde eine andere Figur erfordern'.
